prompt: Write the clause that collapses the rows so there is one row per consumer group: GROUP BY the column c.group_id.
given: Query: SELECT c.group_id, SUM(...) AS total_lag FROM commits c JOIN partitions p ... <your clause> HAVING ...
template:
-- EXPECTED: [["billing", 60], ["zeta", 60], ["fraud", 50], ["analytics", 40]]

-- Tables are loaded for you: partitions(topic, partition_id, log_end_offset) and commits(group_id, topic, partition_id, committed_offset).
SELECT c.group_id,
       SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) AS total_lag
FROM commits c
JOIN partitions p ON p.topic = c.topic AND p.partition_id = c.partition_id
@@BLANK@@
HAVING SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) > 0
ORDER BY total_lag DESC, c.group_id ASC
;
why: GROUP BY collapses the rows to one per consumer group so SUM works per group.
